headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: B handles secrets and APIs while A is an unverified content source with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing repository with no runnable I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. B does expose stdin/stdout and file inputs, but there is no documented shared channel, clipboard, or MCP bridge between them. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or file transfer, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies A-generated text into B's prompt or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two agents, the pathway opens.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or sync folder.
Add a provenance header to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches configuration secrets and academic data, and it can read/write the filesystem plus use allowlisted network egress. A is an unverified content-writing repo with no stated isolation or data handling controls. There is no direct evidence A receives B's secrets, but if outputs or files are shared, sensitive material could leak through B's networked workflows.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or files, B's secrets can be exposed through transferred artifacts.
IF B is pointed at files produced by A that embed secrets or credentials, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared folders.
Review files before B ingests them.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
Restrict B to a dedicated input directory.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning before network calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has read/write filesystem, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; A has no documented runtime capabilities, so direct conflict is not evidenced. However, if A is used as a source tree or artifact generator for B, B can overwrite or mutate shared files in default local-development setups. Uncertainty about shared state pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, B can overwrite A-produced files.
IF A is materialized into a repo that B also modifies, file-level conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Mount A read-only for B.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Snapshot the workspace before B runs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing source with no verification controls, and B exposes agentic ask/search APIs plus a LangGraph subagent model. That makes it plausible for B to treat A's generated text as authoritative input and then act on it. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance checks, so errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as facts or citations, errors can propagate.
IF B's agentic-ask or search pipeline is fed A output without verification, downstream outputs may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add citation checks in B.
Mark A content as untrusted input.
Compare A claims against source documents.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware routing in B.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data and runs in a local development environment; A is an unverified open-source content repository with no residency or retention controls stated. The pair therefore has a compliance gap around secret handling and retention policy mismatch, but there is no evidence of regulated PHI or cross-border residency issues, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B stores secrets or paper data in files shared with A, retention and access controls may be violated.
IF the operator uses the pair for regulated data, the missing residency and certification details become material.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared repos.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
Document retention for B outputs.
Avoid regulated data in this pair.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for secret and data retention handling.
